methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon scrapping four NoVA data centers due to local backlash reveals infrastructure saturation limits even in concentrated tech hubs, potentially stalling the region's AI infrastructure expansion without distributed alternatives emerging elsewhere in Virginia.

signals.title: Roanoke coalition names Texas firm to study AI center plan - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke's formation of 'AI Ready Roanoke' coalition and hiring of external consultants to develop an AI center plan signals intentional effort to build distributed deep capability outside traditional tech corridors, though execution and sustained local capacity-building remain uncertain.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's statewide AI cybersecurity mandate suggests centralized state-level policy capacity concentrated in Richmond leadership, but implementation depth will determine whether this drives distributed capability-building or reinforces dependency on concentrated expertise hubs.

signals.title: Norfolk, Newport News police launch AI tool for non-emergency calls - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk and Newport News police deploying AI tools for non-emergency calls exemplifies shallow, platform-delivered adoption—agencies consume vendor solutions without building internal AI development capacity, creating broad but surface-level distribution.

signals.title: Gleb Tsipursky | Virginia’s AI training needs a first job at the other end - Augusta Free Press
signals.signal_reading: Commentary highlighting the 'first job' problem for AI training graduates reveals a critical gap: Virginia may produce AI-trained workers without corresponding job infrastructure outside NoVA/Richmond, risking talent outmigration and failed workforce investment in underserved regions.
